models.name: RBC Model with an Investment Installation Lag
The RBC Model with a Stock Market

parameters.name: Discount factor (per quarter)
parameters.source: Implied by a data target given the model's structure (since 20 November 2026): the Euler equation on the balanced growth path, 1 + r = (1 + g_X)/β (log utility), with r the average real return on the S&P 500 (the models' stock return is the return on capital) and g_X the trend growth of the default run (measured TFP). Recomputed at each update; King and Rebelo (1999) use 0.984, and 0.988 was used until 20 November 2026.

parameters.name: Relative risk aversion (inverse of the intertemporal elasticity of substitution)
parameters.source: Logarithmic utility in consumption, required for balanced growth with separable utility (King, Plosser and Rebelo, 1988; King and Rebelo, 1999).

parameters.name: Weight of leisure in utility
parameters.source: Implied by the hours target given β: steady-state hours take 20 percent of available time (King and Rebelo, 1999), from the labour-supply condition θC/(1 − N) = (1 − α)Y/N.

parameters.name: Capital’s share of income
parameters.source: King and Rebelo (1999, Table 2).

parameters.name: Depreciation rate (per quarter)
parameters.source: King and Rebelo (1999, Table 2): 10 percent a year.

parameters.name: Trend growth of labour-augmenting technology (per quarter)
parameters.source: Estimated: the linear trend of measured TFP (Fernald, 2014) divided by labour’s share, as in King and Rebelo (1999, section 4.1).

parameters.name: Persistence of technology
parameters.source: Estimated: AR(1) of the deviation of log measured TFP from its linear trend (King and Rebelo, 1999); see Extracting Technology Shocks.

parameters.name: Standard deviation of technology shocks (percent)
parameters.source: Estimated with the persistence: the standard deviation of the AR(1) innovations.

parameters.name: Installation parameter (steady state)
parameters.source: Arthur Galichère’s estimates (may change).

parameters.name: Persistence of installation shocks
parameters.source: Arthur Galichère’s estimates (may change).

parameters.name: Standard deviation of installation shocks (percent)
parameters.source: Arthur Galichère’s estimates (may change); units under review.

parameters.name: Discount factor (per quarter)
parameters.source: Galichère, notes on the canonical New Keynesian model; it implies a real interest rate of about 4 percent a year.

parameters.name: Relative risk aversion
parameters.source: Galichère, notes (logarithmic utility).

parameters.name: Inverse Frisch elasticity of labour supply
parameters.source: Galichère, notes.

parameters.name: Elasticity of substitution between goods
parameters.source: Galichère, notes: a price markup of 10 percent.

parameters.name: Probability of not resetting the price (Calvo)
parameters.source: Galichère, notes: prices last about ten months, in line with Nakamura and Steinsson (2008).

parameters.name: Price-adjustment cost (Rotemberg)
parameters.source: Galichère, notes.

parameters.name: Policy response to inflation
parameters.source: Taylor (1993).

parameters.name: Policy response to the output gap (quarterly rates)
parameters.source: Taylor (1993): 0.5 with annual rates.

parameters.name: Persistence of technology
parameters.source: Estimated on Extracting Shocks for the New Keynesian Model (persistences consistent with the shocks backed out from the data).

parameters.name: Persistence of the weight on the disutility of labour
parameters.source: Estimated on Extracting Shocks for the New Keynesian Model.

parameters.name: Persistence of the discount factor (demand)
parameters.source: Estimated on Extracting Shocks for the New Keynesian Model.

parameters.name: Technology shock (percent)
parameters.source: Estimated: standard deviation of the backed-out innovations.

parameters.name: Labour-preference shock (percent)
parameters.source: Estimated: standard deviation of the backed-out innovations.

parameters.name: Demand shock (percent)
parameters.source: Estimated: standard deviation of the backed-out innovations.

parameters.name: Monetary policy shock (percentage points, annual rate)
parameters.source: Estimated: standard deviation of the backed-out monetary shocks (i.i.d., as in the notes).

targets.name: Consumption share of output
targets.definition: Personal consumption expenditures over GDP, both in current dollars.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Investment share of output
targets.definition: Gross private domestic investment over GDP, both in current dollars.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Government share of output
targets.definition: Government consumption expenditures and gross investment over GDP, in current dollars.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Investment share of private absorption
targets.definition: Investment over consumption plus investment: the investment share of a model economy without government or trade.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Capital–output ratio (years)
targets.definition: Year-end current-cost net stock of private fixed assets (including housing) over annual nominal GDP.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (Fixed Assets Accounts); author's calculation

targets.name: Capital–output ratio, nonresidential (years)
targets.definition: Year-end current-cost net stock of private nonresidential fixed assets over annual nominal GDP.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (Fixed Assets Accounts); author's calculation

targets.name: Hours worked (share of available time)
targets.definition: Average share of available time spent working.
targets.source: King and Rebelo (1999); Prescott (1986)
targets.note: A literature target: the hours series of the site are indices, which do not give a share of time.

targets.name: Growth of real output (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average annualised quarterly growth of real GDP, 400 × Δln Y; per capita: of real GDP per person.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation
targets.note: With constant hours per person in the steady state, per-capita output grows at the rate of labour-augmenting technology, g_X.

targets.name: Growth of real consumption (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average annualised quarterly growth of real personal consumption expenditures.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Real Treasury bill rate (percent a year)
targets.definition: Ex-post real 3-month Treasury bill rate: the bill rate minus GDP-deflator inflation.
targets.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Volatility of the real bill rate (percentage points)
targets.definition: Standard deviation of the quarterly ex-post real bill rate (annual rate).
targets.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Inflation (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average annualised quarterly change in the GDP price index.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation
targets.note: The canonical New Keynesian model has zero steady-state inflation; on its page inflation is taken in deviation from its average since 1954.

targets.name: Federal funds rate (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average effective federal funds rate.
targets.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System via FRED

targets.name: Nominal Treasury bill rate (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average 3-month Treasury bill rate (secondary market).
targets.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System via FRED

targets.name: Price–dividend ratio (annual dividends)
targets.definition: Average of the S&P 500 price over twelve-month dividends.
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation

targets.name: Volatility of the log price–dividend ratio
targets.definition: Standard deviation of the quarterly log price–dividend ratio.
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation

targets.name: Persistence of the log price–dividend ratio (quarterly)
targets.definition: First-order autocorrelation of the quarterly log price–dividend ratio.
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation

targets.name: Dividend yield (percent)
targets.definition: Average of twelve-month dividends over the price of the S&P 500.
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation

targets.name: Real stock return (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average quarterly real total return of the S&P 500, times four.
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation
targets.note: The RBC models' discount factor is set from this target (see the parameters).

targets.name: Volatility of the real stock return (percent a year)
targets.definition: Standard deviation of quarterly real returns, times two (√4).
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation

targets.name: Equity premium (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average quarterly excess return of the S&P 500 over the 3-month Treasury bill, times four (Mehra and Prescott, 1985).
targets.source: Robert J. Shiller, shillerdata.com; author's calculation; Treasury bill rate: Federal Reserve via FRED

targets.name: Dividends as a share of output (percent)
targets.definition: Net corporate dividends (NIPA) over GDP, both in current dollars at annual rates.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Growth of real corporate dividends (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average annualised quarterly growth of real net corporate dividends (NIPA, GDP price index).
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Inflation, NK sample (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average GDP-deflator inflation over the sample of the New Keynesian page (from 1954 Q3), removed from the data there.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED; author's calculation

targets.name: Federal funds rate, NK sample (percent a year)
targets.definition: Average federal funds rate over the sample of the New Keynesian page (from 1954 Q3), removed from the data there.
targets.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System via FRED

targets.name: Firm survival rate (per quarter)
targets.definition: Probability that a firm survives a quarter: the mean over years of (1 − exit)^(1/4), with exit the share of the firms alive in March that exit within the year (8.89 percent a year on average).
targets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Dynamics Statistics; author's calculation
targets.note: Firms all of whose establishments close; see the Business Dynamics page.

targets.name: Persistence of firm survival (per quarter)
targets.definition: Quarterly AR(1) of 100 × ln s_t whose four-quarter sums match the persistence and variance of the HP (6.25) cycle of annual log survival (annual AR(1): -0.06).
targets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Dynamics Statistics; author's calculation

targets.name: Standard deviation of survival shocks (percent)
targets.definition: Innovations of the same quarterly AR(1), in percent of the survival rate (log points × 100).
targets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Dynamics Statistics; author's calculation

targets.name: Firm startup rate (per quarter)
targets.definition: Average annual startup rate (9.97 percent of firms), as a quarterly rate.
targets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Dynamics Statistics; author's calculation

targets.name: Establishment death rate (per quarter)
targets.definition: Private-sector establishments closing permanently each quarter, percent of establishments.
targets.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics

gx.text: the trend growth of labour-augmenting technology in the RBC models (measured TFP, Hicks-neutral; the default run of The Canonical RBC Model)
